item.title: Tesla announces multi-billion-euro expansion of Gigafactory Grünheide
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Tesla has announced plans to invest three billion euros in expanding its factory in Grünheide, Brandenburg. From 2029, the Tesla Cybercab robotaxi is set to be manufactured there. Battery cell production will also be expanded, with construction work scheduled to begin in 2027.

item.title: Vilnius Airport replaces diesel buses with battery-electric buses
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Vilnius Airport is replacing its entire diesel bus fleet for passenger transfers with twelve electric buses from Cobus. The new vehicles will enter service on 16 November. The investment totals €7.2 million, including maintenance and repairs.

item.title: CATL to become market leader in passenger car battery swapping
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: CATL could become the largest battery swap station operator for passenger cars in China next year. The company plans to have 6,000 stations in operation by 2027. According to Chinese industry portals, this should be enough to overtake Nio’s slower-growing battery swapping network.

item.title: US researchers identify electrode drying risk during fast charging
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Researchers at the University of Maryland have found that lithium ions carry solvent molecules with them as they move through a battery. During fast charging, however, the solvent may not flow back quickly enough, causing the positive electrode to dry out and slowing the charging process.

item.title: ASTAG Charge launches with 100 companies across 60 locations
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: The Swiss Commercial Vehicle Association has launched ASTAG Charge, a network that allows members to share their truck charging infrastructure. A total of 100 companies are now participating, providing around 200 charging points for a fleet of 585 electric trucks.

item.title: Lucid cuts cash burn and secures additional $1.75 billion
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Lucid reduced its cash burn by 30 per cent in the third quarter of 2026 compared with the previous quarter. At the same time, Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund, the Public Investment Fund (PIF), is increasing its financing for the electric carmaker by a further $1.75 billion.

item.title: Kempower plans to cut up to 120 jobs worldwide
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Finnish charging station manufacturer Kempower is planning global job cuts, with up to 120 of its 870 positions potentially affected. The company aims to reduce costs in response to challenging market conditions and restructure its organisation.

item.title: Terawatt Infrastructure opens four fleet charging hubs in the US
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: The charging infrastructure provider has added a combined 22 MW of charging capacity across four sites in California, Tennessee, Florida and Texas. According to the company, the new depots can charge more than 3,000 commercial electric vehicles per day.

item.title: Li Auto to enter four new Asian markets and launch right-hand-drive cars
item.dc:creator: Sagar Parikh
item.description: Chinese carmaker Li Auto is expanding its presence in Asia, with plans to enter Hong Kong, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam. The company has also announced its first right-hand-drive models, starting with its flagship Li Mega electric MPV.

item.title: Price jump for Tesla Model Y AWD – base trim no longer available
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: After just over nine months, the entry-level version of the Tesla Model Y AWD has vanished from the configurator. It was the $41,990 option to get a base trim with dual-motor all-wheel drive. Now, the Model Y AWD starts at the Premium trim for $49,990. With rear-wheel drive, the entry-level model still starts at $39,990.

item.title: Visteon, Shinry and Infineon develop single-stage 22 kW onboard charger
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Visteon-Shinry Power Electronics and Infineon are jointly developing a single-stage onboard charger for electric vehicles. The new architecture supports AC charging at up to 22 kW and uses bidirectional GaN switches to achieve a more compact, less complex design than conventional two-stage systems.

item.title: Denmark plans social EV subsidies from 2028
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Denmark is earmarking DKK 3.9 billion (around €521.7 million) for a climate package aimed at making the transition to sustainable transport socially equitable. From 2028, incentives will help low-income households switch to electric cars, including through subsidised leasing. Purchase subsidies are also being considered.

item.title: Tesla Cybercab for private sale comes without steering wheel but with restrictions
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Tesla is inviting “selected customers” to buy Cybercabs for private use at a price of $29,990. However, the car can only be driven with an additional $299-per-month “Autonomy subscription” and is restricted to Tesla's Robotaxi service areas in Texas and Florida.

item.title: BMW opens battery assembly plant for the new iX5
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: BMW has officially opened its new battery assembly plant in Woodruff, South Carolina, and started series production. The factory assembles the high-voltage batteries for the new BMW iX5, marking an important milestone ahead of the electric SUV's production ramp-up.

item.title: Veolia opens battery black mass recycling plant in France
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Veolia is commissioning a new plant in the Grand Est region of France to process black mass from lithium-ion batteries. Using its own hydrometallurgical process, the company expects to recover more than 90 per cent of the nickel, cobalt and copper contained in the material.

item.title: Canada invests billions in charging infrastructure and grid upgrades
item.dc:creator: Carrie Hampel
item.description: The Canadian government is investing in the expansion of electric vehicle charging and grid infrastructure with investments of just over $634 million. The new investment should roughly double the more than 50,000 chargers supported through existing programs. The EV charging initiative is further supported by the government’s national electricity strategy with over $50 billion to be invested in doubling the capacity of Canada’s grid by 2050.

item.title: Nevoya seals multi-year deal with Meta to deploy 25 electric trucks between California and Arizona.
item.dc:creator: Carrie Hampel
item.description: In the USA, the electric truckload carrier startup Nevoya has announced a multi-year agreement with Meta that supports the deployment of 25 Class 8 battery-electric trucks on Interstate 10 (I-10) between San Bernardino, California and Phoenix, Arizona.

item.title: Legal proceedings should establish whether the BYD Ti7 is a Copy of JLR’s Defender
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: British automaker JLR is taking legal action against Chinese competitor BYD for alleged patent infringements. In August, court bailiffs are said to have seized digital documents from two BYD offices in the Netherlands. In the meantime, a court has since ruled the action unnecessary and ordered the destruction of the data.

item.title: Dacia Sandero electric version expected to achieve around 400 km range
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: It has been clear that the next-generation Dacia Sandero will receive a fully electric variant since 2024. Now, according to a British media report, the electric Sandero is expected to be based on the "RGMP Small" platform and offer a range of around 400 kilometers. The release year is rumored to be 2028.

item.title: Kia to invest around €1.8 billion in new plant in India
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: The South Korean automaker Kia plans to build a second vehicle plant in India, which, like the first factory, will be located in Anantapur in the state of Andhra Pradesh. The facility is expected to produce up to 200,000 vehicles annually — both electric cars and internal combustion engine vehicles.

item.title: May Mobility to convert 10,000 VW ID. Buzz vehicles into robotaxis
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: The VW ID. Buzz is set to become a robotaxi on a large scale. US tech company May Mobility has announced plans to deploy more than 10,000 autonomous units of the electric bus globally by the end of 2031. Initial tests on public roads will begin in early 2027 in the US, with series deliveries to external fleet operators starting in 2028.

item.title: Daimler Buses Italia to supply TUA Abruzzo with 40 new electric buses
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Daimler Buses Italia and STI, an Italian energy and charging infrastructure service provider, have won the tender of regional transport operator TUA Abruzzo in Italy. The order includes 40 electric low-floor city buses with an option for eight additional vehicles, as well as the responsibility for setting up the necessary charging infrastructure at TUA's depot on Via Aterno in Pescara.

item.title: Hyundai explores investment in Posco graphite project in Vietnam
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Hyundai Motor Group is considering an investment in Posco Future M's planned synthetic graphite business in Vietnam. The proposed investment is 100 billion won, (around 67.6 million euros). In return, Hyundai is to receive preferred purchasing rights for the anode material.

item.title: VW launches the ID. ERA 5X in China with pricing
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: The VW ID. ERA 5X costs around 13,530 euros in China at market launch and offers more interior space than a VW ID. Tiguan despite its smaller dimensions. This is made possible by the new Compact Main Platform, which debuts with the ID. ERA 5X. The China SUV can also be equipped with partially automated assistance systems.

item.title: VW’s Scout brand begins production of first test vehicles at new US plant
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Volkswagen's revived US brand Scout has begun assembling the first validation vehicles at its new plant in Blythewood, South Carolina. As the factory is still under construction, it will be several more months before Scout vehicles are running off production lines in series.

item.title: UK funds project for recovering nickel, cobalt and copper
item.dc:creator: Carrie Hampel
item.description: ReOre Technologies, an Altilium Group company focused on recovering critical minerals from mining waste, has announced it will lead a new UK government-backed project to unlock domestic supplies of nickel, cobalt and copper. For the two-year Cascade project, ReOre is collaborating with project partners Aberdeen Minerals and Camborne School of Mines, supported by the Battery Innovation Programme.

item.title: British Gas orders nearly 2,000 VW Transporters, some of which are electric
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles has delivered 1,986 new transporters to British Gas. The fleet includes both electric Transporters and diesel models. The companies have not disclosed the number of purely electric vehicles.

item.title: Mercedes board threatens to close German plants and stop investments in Germany
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Mercedes-Benz is temporarily halting its investments in Germany and putting plants up for sale. The move is a response by management to the protracted negotiations with the union over what Mercedes says are excessively high labor costs. The company's board insists on cuts to keep German production competitive.

item.title: Lucid Air Grand Touring: a long-distance champion with plenty of power
item.dc:creator: Kasimir Hupe
item.description: For two weeks, we travelled with this luxury sedan from California. The Lucid Air impresses with its long-distance capability, an extremely quiet interior, and intuitive controls. However, it also has a few weaknesses that shouldn’t exist at this price point.

item.title: UK depot charging scheme reopens – with reduced funding rate
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: The UK Government has reopened applications for the section round of its Depot Charging Scheme, which provides funding for businesses installing charging infrastructure for electric vans and HGVs. However, the grant rate has been reduced from 70 to 60 per cent of eligible costs.
